title: LLM-to-Config with Deterministic Verifier: sim-to-real and vendor-heterogeneity evaluation (repaired preregistration)
research_question: When the same natural-language intent is realized by an LLM-generated configuration and checked by a deterministic verifier, how large is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction between emulated/synthetic topologies and production-like, vendor-heterogeneous topologies?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary, confirmatory): The paired intent-satisfaction rate (verifier-confirmed) will be at least 15 percentage points lower on production-like vendor-heterogeneous topologies than on emulated/synthetic topologies.

H2 (confirmatory, instrumentation): Deterministic verifier checks will detect >90% of syntactic and straightforward semantic errors on the emulation partition under the preregistered verifier encodings.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do violation-type mixes (syntax vs local-policy vs vendor-specific semantic) differ across vendor strata (IOS, JunOS, FRRouting)?
EQ2: How sensitive are paired differences to the predefined small set of prompt variants (sensitivity analysis)?
EQ3: How often do automated repair iterations (preregistered templates) convert verifier-fails into verifier-passes, stratified by partition?
benchmark_scope: Emulation partition: synthetic topologies generated deterministically from public topology generators (see provenance below).
Community partition (exploratory): community-contributed medium-scale topologies assembled from public corpora referenced in evidence_record_ids.
Production-like partition: topologies synthesized from public configuration corpora and deterministic extraction rules derived from the supplied evidence records (provenance and filtering below).
model_scope: Hosted LLM API(s) permitted by capability_manifest (referred to as hosted-llm-api-v1). Exact model identifier(s) will be recorded in execution metadata.
No local GPU models; all LLM calls go to hosted APIs per capability_manifest.
transformation_scope: Syntactic normalization (vendor-specific canonicalization), vendor-mapping translations (canonical ACL/policy encodings), verifier property encoders, and automated repair-prompt templates.
secondary_estimands: fraction of violations by class (syntax/local-policy/vendor-specific) per partition
repair-conversion rate (proportion of failed→passed after automated repairs)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design: fixed set of N_intents intents (pairs). For each intent we generate exactly two LLM-produced configurations (one targeting an emulation partition topology, one targeting a production-like partition topology) then run deterministic verification checks. Confirmatory N_intents = 250 paired intents (=> 500 LLM-generation tasks). Exploratory discovery items: 100 additional single-topology LLM-generation tasks targeted at the community partition (for vendor-stratified descriptive analyses). Totals derived: 250 intents * 2 trials/intent = 500 confirmatory generation trials; plus 100 discovery trials = 600 generation trials overall. Model-call accounting: per generation trial we preregister up to 2 automated repair iterations after the initial generation (initial + up to 2 repairs = up to 3 model calls per generation trial). Therefore worst-case planned_model_calls = 600 generation trials * 3 model calls/trial = 1800 model calls. All seeds and prompts are frozen pre-execution. Each trial is deterministically assigned a topology and vendor stratum; task-clusters = 3 vendor strata (IOS, JunOS, FRR).
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory estimator: paired binary analysis (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) computed by the registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1'. Primary test: two-sided McNemar / paired-proportion procedure implemented by the analysis executor with 95% CIs. Report exact paired test p-value, absolute difference in percentage points with 95% CI, and effect-size. Secondary analyses: stratified per-vendor paired comparisons and violation-type proportions (descriptive with CIs). Sensitivity analyses: (a) treat generation/verification failures as automatic failures (zero) and rerun primary analysis (registered failed_call_treatment includes both complete_pair_primary and complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity), (b) repeat analysis across the small preregistered prompt-variant set and report variation. All analysis code and inputs will be preserved. No post-hoc exclusions of confirmatory pairs are permitted except for the preregistered automated exclusion rules below.
multiplicity_plan: One primary confirmatory comparison (emulation vs production-like). Up to five secondary hypotheses will be reported; p-values for secondaries will be presented but interpreted as exploratory. If formal secondary confirmatory claims are made, adjust using Bonferroni (m ≤ 5).
missingness_plan: Automated treatments only. If an LLM call fails (API error/timeout) we follow deterministic retry policy (one immediate retry). If retry fails, the pair is handled according to the registered failed_call_treatment: primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' (i.e., exclude incomplete pairs) and a sensitivity analysis treats the incomplete pair as pair-failure (zero). If verifier execution fails (runtime error), the trial is flagged and excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis; a sensitivity analysis treats excluded trials as failures. All exclusions and counts, with deterministic reasons, are logged and disclosed.

benchmark_names: Production-like synthesized partition (public config corpora derivation)
risk_factors: Injected prompt or config fragments (prompt-injection) present in retrieved resources used during prompt construction
Presence of private or sensitive configuration fragments in public corpora used for synthesis
Verifier modelling mismatch for vendor-specific features
detection_procedures: Automated syntactic/semantic filters applied to LLM outputs and synthesized inputs (regex and token-pattern detectors for embedded instructions, 'enable secret', clear-text credentials, private IPs); evidence provenance tagging from source records for all synthesized artifacts.

Deterministic provenance checks: every synthesized production-like topology includes source-record identifiers (from allowed evidence_record_ids) and a hashing provenance fingerprint; items failing provenance checks are excluded.
Verifier-consistency checks: run each verified property under two encodings (primary encoding and an alternate encoding rule set); disagreements are flagged deterministically.
item_flagging_rules: Flag and exclude any synthesized config containing credential-like tokens, private-address blocks not deterministically anonymized, or clearly copy-matched copyrighted fragments identified via exact-hash matching against a denylist.

Flag any LLM output where embedded instruction-like tokens (patterns from prompt-injection literature in evidence) appear; treat flagged outputs as excluded from primary analysis and included in a contamination-reporting appendix.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis. Two sensitivity treatments are preregistered: (A) re-run primary analysis with all flagged items treated as failures; (B) re-run with flagged items removed (primary). Both results reported.
residual_uncertainty: Automated detectors are imperfect; flagged/unflagged trade-offs are quantified in the contamination report.
Synthesis from public corpora may still not represent proprietary vendor idiosyncrasies (addressed as noncritical external-validity limitation).

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended balanced-power scenario. Confirmatory N_pairs = 250; exploratory discovery trials = 100; task clusters = 3 vendor strata (IOS, JunOS, FRR).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Total planned_model_calls (1800) fits under the capability manifest limit (max planned model calls 10000). All compute is via hosted APIs and CPU-only deterministic verification (Batfish-equivalent) using available CPU execution. No human annotation is required.

budget_scenarios.description: Lower-budget, lower-power scenario. Confirmatory N_pairs = 150; exploratory discovery trials = 50; task clusters = 3.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Conservative call budget for constrained API allowances; still executable within capability_manifest. Reduced power relative to recommended scenario.

budget_scenarios.description: High-powered scenario for increased precision. Confirmatory N_pairs = 400; exploratory discovery trials = 200; task clusters = 3.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Matches the candidate's original estimated_model_calls (3000) and remains within capability_manifest maximum planned calls. Higher sample yields greater power for small effects and more robust stratified analyses.

power_plan.target_effect: 15 percentage points absolute difference (production-like minus emulation)
power_plan.clustering_unit: intent-pair (each pair = same intent on emulation and production-like topology)
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate McNemar/paired-proportion sample-size calculation using two-sided alpha=0.05. Calculation used assumed baseline emulation pass rate p1=0.90 and paired discordant proportion consistent with a 15% absolute reduction; standard normal approximation. Detailed calculation script recorded in preregistration artifacts.
assumptions: Baseline emulation verifier-confirmed pass rate ≈ 0.90 (consistent with literature C2/C3) for the chosen intents.
Discordant-pair rate consistent with a 15 percentage-point shift; independence across intent-pairs is assumed for power calculation.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: Under the above assumptions, required paired N ≈ 230; recommended confirmatory N = 250 to provide >80% power allowing modest deviation from assumptions. If actual emulation baseline is lower, detectable effect increases; the high-budget scenario (N=400) reduces MDE substantially.
sensitivity_analyses: Treat incomplete pairs as failures (zero) and re-run primary estimator (registered failed_call_treatment 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity').
Repeat primary analysis across the preregistered small set of prompt variants (up to 3 variants) and report variability in paired differences.
Recompute primary estimator excluding any items flagged by contamination detectors vs treating flagged items as failures; report both.

transformation_families: alternate_property_encodings (secondary verifier encodings for consistency checks)
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip check: generated config -> vendor parser -> canonical representation -> re-emitted config; compare semantics via header-space/reachability on a small deterministic emulated topology; mismatch rates recorded.
Alternate-encoding agreement: for each property, compare primary and alternate encodings in verifier; record disagreement rate.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject any generated config that fails vendor-parser (syntax) deterministically.
Reject any generated config that contains disallowed tokens (credential-like strings) per regex denylist.
Reject items that fail provenance hashing or that match denylist copyright fingerprints.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Audit = deterministic 10% sample of all generated configs selected by an intent-id hash function (no human annotation). Audit executes an expanded automated static-analysis battery (additional parsers and property encodings) and records discrepancies automatically.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Vendor mapping tables and canonicalization scripts are validated by unit tests against public examples drawn from the evidence_record_ids corpora; test-suite results recorded and preserved.
residual_risks: Automated equivalence checks cannot perfectly capture complex vendor-specific dynamic behaviors (e.g., proprietary feature interactions).
Audit is automated and cannot substitute for human expert adjudication; therefore some nuanced semantic errors may remain undetected.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External-validity limitation: publicly synthesized production-like topologies and configs may not capture proprietary vendor idiosyncrasies; this restricts generalization to private production networks (explicitly bounded in claims).

Verifier fidelity: deterministic verifiers may under- or over-approximate certain vendor-specific behaviors; this is mitigated by alternate-encoding agreement checks but remains a modelling limitation.

Hosted-model API operational constraints (rate limits, latency) could reduce realized throughput; preregistered retries and the planned model-call budgets are designed to operate within capability_manifest limits, but real-world API throttling remains a noncritical execution risk.
Automated PII/copyright detectors are imperfect; residual sensitive fragments might remain undetected despite provenance hashing and denylist filtering.
